bib.title: Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs: A Survey

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs: A Survey". Rongwu Xu, Zehan Qi, Zhijiang Guo, Cunxiang Wang, Hongru Wang, Yue Zhang, Wei Xu. Affiliations: Tsinghua University (Xu, Qi, W. Xu), University of Cambridge (Guo), Westlake University (Wang, Zhang), CUHK (H. Wang). Xu, Qi and Guo are the leading authors; Xu and Qi contributed equally. The extraction prints "arXiv:2403.08319v2 [cs.CL] 22 Jun 2024" and names no conference or journal, so treat it as an arXiv preprint (v2) unless you verify a venue elsewhere. Year: 2024.

COVERAGE: 121,215 of 121,215 chars, all 27 pages. Pages 1-9 hold the body, the limitations and the ethics statement. The references fill the rest. The appendix (A.1-A.3, Tables 2 and 3) is at the end and I read it fully. I skimmed the references only for origins. Nothing was skipped.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: The survey defines three conflict types by where the clashing knowledge sits. Context is user prompt, dialogue history and retrieved documents. Memory is the model's parameters.
  number: none (3 types)
  setup: Taxonomy for LLMs, rooted in open-domain QA work. The survey searched papers from 2021 onward.
  quote: "we categorize three distinct types of knowledge conflicts" ... "context-memory conflict (CM, § 2)" ... "inter-context conflict (IC, § 3)" ... "intra-memory conflict (IM, § 4)"
  where: p1-2, Fig 1
- Claim: Context-memory conflict has two causes. Temporal misalignment makes the context right and the memory stale. Misinformation pollution makes the context wrong.
  number: none
  setup: General LLM / RAG.
  quote: "For the former, the up-to-date contextual information is considered accurate. Conversely, for the latter, the contextual information contains misinformation and is therefore considered incorrect."
  where: §2.1 Remarks, p3-4
- Claim: The usual fixes for temporal misalignment each bring a cost. Knowledge editing adds intra-memory conflict. RAG cannot avoid conflict because the parameters stay unchanged. Continual learning forgets and is expensive.
  number: none
  setup: Survey statement.
  quote: "KE can bring in side effects of knowledge conflict, leading to knowledge inconsistency (i.e., a sort of intra-memory conflict)... For RAG, it is inevitable to encounter knowledge conflicts since the model's parameters are not updated"
  where: §2.1
- Claim: Misinformation can enter through retrieved web corpora and through user conversations. The survey names prompt injection and sycophancy as aggravating factors.
  number: none
  quote: "adversaries can leverage techniques such as prompt injection attacks" ; "the model's tendency to align with user opinions, a.k.a., sycophancy"
  where: §2.1
- Claim: There is no definitive rule for whether a model prefers context or memory. Coherent, logical, convincing knowledge tends to win.
  number: none
  setup: Cross-paper synthesis. Early work (Longpre 2021) found over-reliance on memory. Chen 2022 found context dominates when passages are multiple. Tan 2024 found a preference for LLM-generated (parametric) context. Xie 2023 found models are receptive to coherent evidence but show confirmation bias.
  quote: "No definitive rule exists for whether a model prioritizes contextual or parametric knowledge. Yet, knowledge that is semantically coherent, logical, and compelling is typically favored by models over generic conflicting information."
  where: §2.2 Remarks, p4-5
- Claim: How you build the conflict changes the result. Entity substitution makes passages less coherent and pushes models toward memory. LLM-generated conflicts push models toward context.
  number: ">60% parametric" vs ">80% context"
  setup: Xie et al. 2023 as compiled by the survey. ChatGPT, GPT-4, PaLM2, Qwen, Llama2 and Vicuna on PopQA and StrategyQA.
  quote: "For entity substitution-based counter-memory, only ChatGPT, GPT-4, and PaLM2 over 60% probability of choosing parametric memory. For generation-based counter-memory, all models have more than 80% probability of choosing context knowledge."
  where: Table 2, p~20
- Claim: Misinformation in context sharply degrades QA accuracy, and multi-turn counter-memory shifts model beliefs.
  number: "up to 87%"; "20.7% to 78.2%"
  setup: Pan et al. 2023b: ChatGPT on NQ-1500 and CovidNews. Xu et al. 2023: ChatGPT, GPT-4, Llama2, Vicuna on Farm, BoolQ, TruthfulQA, NQ.
  quote: "Misinformation in the context can lead to a significant degradation (up to 87%) in the performance." ; "as the number of counter-memory context increases, the cumulative proportion of belief alteration of LLMs spans from 20.7% to 78.2%"
  where: Table 2
- Claim: The survey sorts solutions by their goal: faithful to context, discriminating misinformation (faithful to memory), disentangling sources, or improving factuality. It says the goals contradict each other because the methods do not separate the two causes, and blind faithfulness to either side is undesirable.
  number: none
  quote: "Current mitigation approaches have contradicted goals because they do not distinguish between the two causes of knowledge conflict when considering conflict scenarios. Blindly being 'faithful' to context or knowledge is undesirable."
  where: §2.3 Remarks
- Claim: The survey ties solutions to timing. Pre-hoc means adjusting before conflicts arise. Post-hoc means adjusting after.
  number: none
  quote: "The key distinction between them lies in whether adjustments are made before or after potential conflicts arise. Another interpretation is that a pre-hoc strategy is proactive while a post-hoc one is reactive."
  where: p2, footnote 1
- Claim: Inter-context conflict has two causes, misinformation and outdated information. The survey says they affect models differently and need separate analysis. It singles out documents with different timestamps when the prompt names a time period.
  number: none
  quote: "Conflicts in context frequently arise between misinformation and accurate information, as well as between outdated and updated information."
  where: §3.1, p5
- Claim: Behaviour under inter-context conflict. Models favour evidence that matches their memory, the answer supported by more documents, higher-popularity entities, and evidence that is relevant to the query. They are sensitive to evidence order. They weigh relevance over the stylistic credibility cues humans use. They struggle as conflicting hops increase.
  number: none
  setup: Chen 2022 (FiD, NQ-Open, TriviaQA), Xie 2023, Wan 2024, Jin 2024a.
  quote: "these models demonstrate a significant sensitivity to the order in which data is introduced" ; "existing models heavily prioritize the relevance of a document to the query but often overlook stylistic features that humans consider important, such as the presence of scientific references or a neutral tone"
  where: §3.2
- Claim: Conflicting evidence or noise lowers performance, and LLMs detect contradictions poorly except GPT-4.
  number: ">10%"; ">20% at noise >0.8"; ">70%" vs "<50%"
  setup: Jin 2024a (ChatGPT, Llama2, Baichuan2, FLAN-UL2, FLAN-T5). Chen 2023b (RGB benchmark). Li 2023a (CONTRADOC).
  quote: "ChatGPT's recall declined the least, but more than 10%." ; "When the noise rate exceeds 0.8, the performance of all models decreases by more than 20%." ; "gpt4 has a more than 70% probability of determining the occurrence of a contradiction, while other models are less than 50%."
  where: Table 2
- Claim: Intra-memory conflict means different answers to semantically equivalent inputs. It has three causes at three stages: training-corpus bias (the fundamental one), stochastic decoding, and knowledge editing.
  number: none
  quote: "These factors respectively pertain to the training phase, the inference phase, and subsequent knowledge refinement." ; "training corpus bias stands out as the fundamental catalyst"
  where: §4.1
- Claim: Intra-memory inconsistency is measurable and large. The survey notes cross-lingual inconsistency does not improve with model size.
  number: "13%"; "32% on FaVIQ"; "15.7% to 22.9%"; "barely 50-60%"; "40% disparity"
  setup: Zhao 2023b (GPT-4 on commonsense QA, and FaVIQ). Mündler 2023 (self-contradiction in GPT-4, ChatGPT, Llama2, Vicuna). Elazar 2021 (BERT-family consistency). Li 2023c (probe vs generation accuracy).
  quote: "even GPT-4 exhibits a notable inconsistency rate of 13% when applied to Commonsense Question-Answering tasks" ; "LLMs create contradictory content, with a probability of between 15.7% and 22.9%. More powerful models create fewer contradictory results." ; "a substantial 40% disparity between the knowledge probe accuracy and the generation accuracy" ; "no observed improvement in cross-lingual consistency with increased model size"
  where: §4.2; Table 2
- Claim: Reported gains of mitigations are not comparable across papers.
  number: "54.4%" and "128%" (CAD); "about 80% F1" and ">5%" (discriminator)
  setup: Table 3, compiled from original papers, no new experiments. CAD (Shi 2023a): GPT-Neo 20B on MemoTrap and NQ-Swap. Hong 2023: ChatGPT and FiD on NQ and TQA. Pan 2023b: >10% accuracy gain.
  quote: "Their method improves GPT-Neo 20B by 54.4% on Memotrap and by 128% on NQ-SWAP where LLMs need to adhere to the given context." ; "It is imperative, however, to approach this analysis with caution, recognizing that original authors may have employed different datasets, LLM variants, or even pursued contrasting objectives."
  where: Table 3; A.1
- Claim: A mechanistic finding: late-layer "memory heads" recall internal knowledge and "context heads" read from the context. Pruning them resolves conflicts without updating parameters (Jin 2024b).
  number: none
  quote: "memory heads can recall knowledge from internal memory, and context heads can retrieve knowledge from the external context. Inspired by this, Pruning Head via Path Patching is introduced"
  where: §5 Explainability

Solutions by type (verbatim names, for the note)
- CM, faithful to context: KAFT (Li 2022a, fine-tuning with counterfactual and irrelevant contexts), TrueTeacher, K-DIAL, OPIN (opinion-based prompts and counterfactual demos), CAD (contrastive decoding with and without context), CuQA (plug-in), ICLM (pre-training), fact-duration prediction (Zhang and Choi 2023).
- CM, discriminating misinformation: vigilant prompting (Pan 2023b, Xu 2023), CAR query augmentation (Weller 2022), a trained discriminator (Hong 2023).
- CM, disentangling sources: DisentQA, Wang 2023h (detect conflict, locate segments, give distinct answers).
- CM, improving factuality: COMBO, CD2.
- IC, eliminating conflict: PCNN, Pielka 2022, Wu 2022, Chern 2023 (tool-using fact-checking), Leite 2023. IC, improving robustness: Hong 2023, Weller 2022.
- IM, improving consistency: Elazar 2021 consistency loss, Li 2023d, CRM, ConCoRD, Zhao 2023b. IM, improving factuality: DoLa, ITI.

LIMITS
- Authors concede they may have missed recent or less relevant findings. The Limitations section is short.
- The tables were compiled from other papers with "no computational experiments". The authors warn the numbers are not comparable.
- Most analyses use artificially built conflicts (entity substitution or LLM-generated), and the findings "might not easily transfer to practical applications". Real-world RAG conflicts are understudied; Wan 2024 is the exception.
- No one-size-fits-all solution exists. Existing methods "assume a prior" or cover one subclass.
- Evaluation is mostly QA (NQ-Open, TriviaQA, PopQA, StrategyQA), with little on downstream tasks such as legal, medical or financial. English and text only.
- Little work covers how intra-memory conflict interacts with the other two types. Internal mechanisms are underexplored.
- Dated: models covered are ChatGPT, GPT-4, PaLM2, Llama2 and Vicuna, with coverage to early 2024. Table 1 note says CM datasets depend on the tested model's own knowledge, so pick the subset that matches the model.
- Typo in the source: the §4.2 Remarks says "inter-memory conflict", meaning intra-memory.

BUILDS ON: Longpre et al. (2021, entity-based conflicts); Chen et al. (2022, multi-passage conflicts); Xie et al. (2023, adaptive chameleon / confirmation bias); Elazar et al. (2021, consistency); Lewis et al. (2020, RAG). The survey says it extends the brief treatment in Feng et al. (2023), which splits conflicts into external and internal.

CODE: none.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p1): three conflict types in a World Cup example. Retrieved documents (Germany, Brazil), the user prompt and the model's memory (Italy, Brazil) clash. It is the fastest way to see context-memory, inter-context and intra-memory side by side.
- Fig 2 (p2): causes lead to conflict, which leads to behaviours, with pre-hoc and post-hoc solutions. Shows the survey's framing of conflict as a nexus.
- Fig 3 (p3): full taxonomy tree (causes, analysis, solutions per type, pre-hoc/post-hoc markers).
- Table 1 (p3): datasets with approach (Sub/Gen/Hum), size and conflict type. Examples: Xie 2023, 20,091 CM; Pan 2023a, 52,189 IC; ParaRel, 328 IM.
- Tables 2-3 (appendix): quantitative impact and mitigation results.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The text extraction has some glued words in Fig 1 only (lost spaces). Page numbers for tables are approximate, since I worked from character offsets: Table 2 and Table 3 start at about char 117,000 to 120,000. Venue is not printed in the PDF text. The figure extraction script listed captions for Figs 1-3 only. The extracted text is saved at /tmp/xu_kc.txt.
